note: The main banks were taken as Moldova's three largest by assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): maib, Moldindconbank and Victoriabank. Victoriabank: its credit card list and its STAR Card and STAR Card Platinum pages, read 2026-10-30; its other cards in that list are debit cards or overdrafts on salary and social accounts, not written. Both bear a floating 16.19% a year with up to 56 days of grace; each card linked to the account costs nothing in its first year, which is introductory, then 100 lei a year (STAR Card) or 1,000 lei (Platinum). Cash at ATMs and counter POS costs 2%. The pages state no minimum payment, foreign-currency fee or late charge. maib and Moldindconbank answered with bot checks on the earlier reading and weren't retried. Wave 4 (30 October 2026): OTP Bank (Moldova) was added as the next large bank whose card terms are published at a plain address (maib and Moldindconbank sat behind bot checks on the earlier reading and weren't retried). OTP Bank's card tariffs (dated 30 October 2026) and its Mastercard Standard NEOS and Visa Gold Credit pages, read 30 October 2026: both in lei, free to hold, with a grace period of up to 60 days on purchases; each page's representative example gives a fixed rate of 21.00% a year, written as the rate; the monthly repayment is at least 5% of the credit used (the Visa Gold's page adds the interest); a cash withdrawal at OTP's own ATMs costs 1.9% plus 0.60 euros (the euro part, in another currency, isn't modelled; other banks' 3% plus 0.90 euros isn't written). The premium Mastercard Gold, Platinum and World Elite credit cards, issued only within the Top Affluent packages, aren't written; no foreign transaction or late fee is stated. No minimum payment is published for Victoriabank's STAR Card and STAR Card Platinum; tried: the STAR Card page (read again 2026-10-30; its example gives an instalment over 5 years, not a least payment), and the earlier reading of both card pages, which found none.
